purpose: Define canonical source roles, their permitted authority, and deterministic reconciliation rules when multiple artifacts describe related semantic surfaces.

definition.meaning: Defines active canonical semantics for its identity when active.

membership_registry.meaning: Enumerates membership/registration facts; does not redefine member semantics.
membership_registry.may_be_semantic_authority: only for the registry membership surface it explicitly owns

boundary_master.meaning: Declares boundaries, entry points or top-level active references; does not absorb child semantics.
boundary_master.may_be_semantic_authority: only for the boundary/bootstrap surface it explicitly owns

reconciliation.meaning: Makes explicit how already-authoritative sources are reconciled; it must not invent missing domain semantics.
reconciliation.may_be_semantic_authority: only for the reconciliation rule itself

historical_or_migration.meaning: Historical or migration evidence; not active semantic authority.

derived_projection.meaning: Read-only derived view of canonical semantics.

precedence_rules: Explicit active semantic definition beats historical_or_migration evidence for active meaning.
Definition semantics are not overridden by a membership_registry that merely lists the definition.
Boundary masters declare entry/boundary surfaces but do not redefine child semantics.
Derived projections never override their canonical sources.
Reconciliation rules may select among explicitly scoped authoritative sources only when the selection rule itself is canonical and deterministic.
No generic newest-file, highest-version, deepest-directory, filename, or timestamp heuristic determines authority.
value.conflict_rule: If two simultaneously authoritative sources assert incompatible facts within the same semantic scope and no explicit reconciliation rule resolves them, the result is an explicit semantic gap and the affected surface cannot be locked.
value.duplication_rule: Duplicated semantic facts across multiple authoritative sources are discouraged because they create drift risk; prefer one semantic definition plus references/composition.
value.topic_rule: Topic membership and Topic composition are source-neutral grouping mechanisms and do not affect source-role authority.

value.purpose: Group canonical source-role, precedence and reconciliation semantics.

invariants.rule: Every canonical artifact declares its source_role explicitly.
Derived projections never become canonical semantic authority.
Historical/migration artifacts do not participate as active semantic definitions.

hard_gates.condition: Canonical artifact has no explicit valid source_role.
Authority is selected using timestamp, file order, path depth or newest-file heuristics.
A derived projection overrides an authoritative semantic definition.
A membership registry silently redefines semantics owned by a member definition.
Boundary Master is treated as semantic owner of child definitions solely because it references them.
Conflicting simultaneously authoritative facts exist in the same semantic scope without explicit reconciliation.

references.purpose: Active/historical state participates in source authority.
Source authority is resolved against explicit canonical identities.
Unresolved source conflicts become explicit semantic gaps.

semantics.identity_rule: This member gives an exact owner-scoped identity to the literal Flow token without adding semantics beyond the owning Flow reference field and the preserved source literal.
semantics.interpretation_rule: Consumers may use this identity as an opaque declared Flow symbol. No meaning may be inferred from spelling, whitespace, filename, path or similarity to another symbol.
semantics.authority_rule: A Flow symbol is descriptive/causal model data only and never grants runtime authority, capability, ownership or execution permission.
semantics.scope_rule: Identity is scoped semantically to the defining contract; identical source literals in another contract or another Flow-ref role are not automatically the same semantic identity.
